The teacher marked every grammar error in my essay but did not always write the correction. _____. Finding the correct form myself helped me notice repeated patterns.

options.B: The teacher rewrote the entire essay
options.C: I was told never to revise the text
options.D: Instead, the symbols in the margin showed what type of mistake I had made

explanation: The correct sentence creates the strongest logical connection between the ideas before and after the gap.

question_text:
Choose the sentence that best completes the text.

We originally planned a thirty-question survey. _____. The shorter version produced more complete responses.

options.A: After a pilot test, we removed questions that did not support the main research goal
options.C: Participants asked for more complicated wording

explanation: The correct sentence creates the strongest logical connection between the ideas before and after the gap.

question_text:
Choose the sentence that best completes the text.

I thought I needed to feel motivated before beginning revision. _____. Now I start with a five-minute task, and motivation often appears after I have begun.

options.A: Revision became impossible after five minutes
options.B: Waiting for the right mood usually meant I delayed the work
options.C: My exam date changed every day

explanation: The correct sentence creates the strongest logical connection between the ideas before and after the gap.

question_text:
Choose the sentence that best completes the text.

The event page clearly listed the date and location, but few people registered. _____. Sign-ups increased once we explained what participants would actually do there.

options.A: The venue had become impossible to reach
options.B: The date was hidden from visitors
options.C: Visitors still could not tell why the event might be useful to them
options.D: Registration was closed before the page was published

explanation: The correct sentence creates the strongest logical connection between the ideas before and after the gap.

question_text:
Choose the sentence that best completes the text.

Maks copied every new expression into a notebook with a translation. _____. Adding one personal example sentence made the expressions easier to use later.

options.A: The notebook contained too few pages
options.C: He decided to learn no new expressions
options.D: He noticed that he could recognise many items but could not produce them in conversation

explanation: The correct sentence creates the strongest logical connection between the ideas before and after the gap.

question_text: By the time we reached the station, the train _____.
explanation: Past Perfect shows that the train left before another past event.

question_text: If I _____ more time yesterday, I would have checked the final paragraph again.
explanation: Third Conditional uses if + Past Perfect for an unreal past condition.

question_text: The results _____ on the school website tomorrow morning.
explanation: The results receive the action, so a future passive form is required.

question_text: She avoided _____ her phone while she was revising.
explanation: Avoid is followed by a gerund.

question_text: The student _____ presentation won the competition thanked the whole team.
explanation: Whose expresses possession before the noun presentation.

question_text: You _____ submit the form today; the deadline has been extended until Friday.
explanation: Don't have to expresses lack of necessity.

question_text: I have been interested in design _____ I was at primary school.
explanation: Since introduces the starting point of an action or state continuing to the present.

question_text: There are _____ students in the library today than there were yesterday.
explanation: Fewer is used with plural countable nouns.

question_text: He said that he _____ the document the previous evening.
explanation: An action completed before the reported past moment is commonly backshifted to Past Perfect.

question_text: This is _____ route to the city centre during rush hour.
explanation: The superlative is required when selecting one route as the highest degree in a group.

question_text: I'd rather you _____ me before changing the shared file.
explanation: Would rather + subject commonly uses a past form for a present or future preference.

question_text: Rarely _____ such a clear explanation of this rule.
explanation: A negative-frequency adverb at the beginning triggers subject-auxiliary inversion.

question_text: I _____ for this exam all week, so I am taking a short break tonight.
explanation: Present Perfect Continuous describes an activity continuing over a period up to now.

question_text: Unless you _____ your email address correctly, you will not receive the confirmation.
explanation: Unless takes a present form when referring to a real future condition.

question_text: The classroom needs _____ before the next group arrives.
explanation: Need + gerund can have a passive meaning: the classroom needs to be cleaned.

question_text: The teacher to _____ I spoke recommended a different book.
explanation: Whom can follow a preposition when referring to a person as the object.

question_text: You _____ have checked the attachment before sending the email.
explanation: Should have + past participle expresses criticism or regret about a past action.

question_text: We arrived _____ the airport earlier than expected.
explanation: Arrive at is used for specific places such as an airport or station.

question_text: _____ of the two proposals fully solves the problem.
explanation: Neither refers to not one and not the other of two items.

question_text: She asked me whether I _____ free the following day.
explanation: Would expresses future in the past in reported speech.

question_text: The new rule will come into _____ at the beginning of October.
explanation: Come into effect means begin to apply officially.

question_text: I need to _____ up on the vocabulary from last term before the test.
explanation: Brush up on means refresh or improve knowledge you already had.

question_text: The instructions were clear and _____, so we finished the setup quickly.
explanation: An adjective is needed to describe the instructions.

question_text: After a long discussion, the group finally reached an _____.
explanation: A noun is required after an.

question_text: You should take travel time into _____ when planning the day.
explanation: Take something into account means consider it.

question_text: We ran _____ of time and had to leave the final question unanswered.
explanation: Run out of means have no more of something left.

question_text: The article raises an important _____ about the use of personal data.
explanation: Raise an issue is a common collocation meaning introduce an important topic or problem.

question_text: The new menu is much more _____; customers can find what they need in seconds.
explanation: User-friendly means easy for people to use.

question_text: The school plans to _____ a mentoring programme for new students.
explanation: Launch a programme means start it officially.

question_text: I came _____ an old practice test while organising my files.
explanation: Come across means find or meet something by chance.

question_text: Regular speaking practice made a _____ improvement to her confidence.
explanation: An adjective is needed before improvement.

question_text: The organiser apologised for the _____ caused by the delayed start.
explanation: A noun is required after the.

question_text: Please _____ attention to the final sentence of the question.
explanation: Pay attention is the fixed collocation.

question_text: The teacher pointed _____ that the example did not support our conclusion.
explanation: Point out means draw attention to a fact or problem.

question_text: We completed the project ahead of _____.
explanation: Ahead of schedule means earlier than planned.

question_text: Her answer showed a good _____ of the main argument.
explanation: A noun is required after a good.

question_text: We need to _____ down the list to the three strongest ideas.
explanation: Narrow down means reduce the number of choices.

question_text: The final presentation was both informative and visually _____.
explanation: An adjective is required after visually to describe the presentation.

question_text: The course did not live up _____ the description on the website.
explanation: Live up to means be as good as expected or promised.

question_text: Students are encouraged to make _____ of the free mock tests before the exam.
explanation: Make use of means use something that is available.
